chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Zurārah, who said:

I saw a son of Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام during the lifetime of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام; he was called ʿAbdullāh, a weaned child who had begun to walk. So I said to him, “O boy, who is this beside you?” referring to a mawlā of theirs. He said, “This is my mawlā.” The mawlā said to him jokingly, “I am not your mawlā.” He replied, “That is evil for you.”

Then a stab was made during the boy’s funeral, and he died. So he was taken out in a basket to al-Baqīʿ. Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام came out wearing a yellow khazz cloak, a yellow khazz turban, and a yellow khazz mantle. He went walking to al-Baqīʿ while leaning on me, and the people were offering him condolences for the son of his son.
When he reached al-Baqīʿ, Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام stepped forward and performed the salat over him, pronouncing four takbirs over him. Then he ordered that he be buried, and so he was buried.

Then he took my hands and moved aside with me, then said: “He would not perform salat over children. Rather, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to order concerning them, and they would be buried one after another behind [the others], and salat would not be performed over them. I only performed salat over him for the sake of the people of al-Madīnah, lest they say: ‘They do not perform salat over their children.’”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, cited here as precedent
key_terms.الْأَطْفَالِ: young children, in the context of funeral salat rulings
key_terms.فَصَلَّى: he performed salat, referring here to the funeral prayer
key_terms.فَكَبَّرَ: he pronounced the takbirs in the funeral prayer
key_terms.مَوْلَايَ: my mawlā, indicating a bond of affiliation or service in context

ai.seo_question: Is salat al-janazah performed over young children according to this hadith from al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This hadith relates the death and funeral of a young child from the family of Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام in the presence of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام. It also conveys a legal point: that salat was not ordinarily performed over small children, and that in this case Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام did so to avoid public reproach from the people of al-Madīnah.
